cases.title: A fault while the committed boundary is being copied produces no checkpoint at all.
cases.statement: The capture copy refuses before any committed state was copied, so no document exists, no artifact was published and the world that was being captured keeps running.

cases.title: A fault while the captured document is being published leaves the previously stored document as the stored one.
cases.statement: The publication is refused and its temporary artifact removed, so a reader still sees the previously verified document or nothing at all and never a partial one.

cases.title: A fault while the destination composition, recipes and references are being rebuilt builds no destination.
cases.statement: The destination's reference tables were never rebuilt, so nothing was staged, exposed or reserved beyond the attempt and the faulted source world is unchanged.

cases.title: A fault at either reach of the postwrite boundary destroys the staged destination instead of exposing it.
cases.statement: Both reaches of the postwrite boundary are covered - after the staged world was written to and as the validated world is about to be published - and each leaves the same observable result: the staged world was destroyed rather than published, so no epoch, revision or session became reachable and the source world stays untouched.

cases.title: A fault either side of the outbox append keeps an obligation undeliverable until it is durable.
cases.statement: An obligation is handed to its destination only after its frame is durable, so a fault before the append refuses the commit rather than delivering an obligation no journal holds.

cases.title: A fault between handing an obligation over and recording the attempt is the acknowledgement-loss window.
cases.statement: The obligation stays open and a redelivery carries the same external idempotency key, so the destination applies at most one mutation.

cases.title: A fault either side of the acknowledgement leaves the obligation redeliverable or settled, never both.
cases.statement: An acknowledgement is persisted before it is applied, so a fault before it leaves the obligation redeliverable and a fault after it leaves the obligation settled with the destination effect unchanged.

cases.title: A restart recovers from the stored document alone or produces no world at all.
cases.statement: A restart carries no in-process state, so the verified document either produces a new session or, when it is absent or corrupt, no world at all, and the faulted session is never resumed.
